candidate.scope: standalone prequantized diagnostic only; never model-routed
candidate.design: A 256-thread, eight-wave workgroup computed a 128-output x 128-token tile over K256. It packed BF16 activations into source-compatible K-major D4 blocks, cooperatively gathered byte-lossless resident Q8T16 slabs into llama.cpp's padded row-major shared weight tile, issued two signed integer-WMMA K16 operations per 32-K scale interval, and accumulated scaled products in FP32 before BF16 output.

correctness.red: Collection failed because no callable/registered MMQ128 D4 wrapper existed.
correctness.green_command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1100 HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/hipengine-hipcc-version-lcp3.txt PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest tests/test_gguf_q8_0_t16_wmma_prefill.py -q -k lcp3d -vv

microbench.protocol: W7900 HIP events, eight cycling Q8T16 weight copies, three warmup cycles, 60 rotated measured repetitions per mode, cached builds. Modes were production two-wave FP16 WMMA, prequantized MMQ128 body, and D4 quantization plus MMQ128 body.

decision.reason: The source-scale tile geometry is not sufficient over resident Q8T16. T16 stores quants K-major inside 16-column slabs, so populating llama.cpp's output-major packed-int shared tile requires four byte gathers and packing per int32 weight fragment. The body is 2.19x production even before quantization; D4 packing is not the blocker.
decision.profiler: Skipped after the prospectively frozen primary body gate failed.
decision.source_disposition: Removed the candidate kernel, quantizer, wrappers, registry key, and tests; production source/defaults are unchanged.
decision.next: Do not attempt another T16-to-MMQ shared transpose. Any further dense-Q8 MMQ work must first use a source-compatible output-major/raw replacement layout and account for decode and memory tradeoffs, or close dense-Q8 and move to the next measured family.
